@tbl-stan-jags-proportion puts the two programs beside the [posterior](bayesian-inference.qmd#def-posterior) of [the Beta-Bernoulli example](bayesian-inference.qmd#exm-beta-bernoulli),
whose Beta parameters come from the number of successes and failures:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-stan-jags-proportion
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior of the proportion from JAGS, Stan and the Beta posterior"
#| echo: false
summarize_draws <- function(draws) {
  c(
    mean = mean(draws),
    stats::quantile(draws, c(0.025, 0.975))
  )
}
shape1 <- 1 + sum(y)
shape2 <- 1 + length(y) - sum(y)
beta_posterior <- c(
  mean = shape1 / (shape1 + shape2),
  stats::qbeta(c(0.025, 0.975), shape1, shape2)
)
comparison <- rbind(
  JAGS = summarize_draws(p_draws),
  Stan = summarize_draws(stan_draws),
  Beta = beta_posterior
)
knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 3, col.names = c("Mean", "2.5%", "97.5%"))
```

Stan's split [potential scale reduction factor](mcmc.qmd#def-psrf) is
`r round(stan_summary[1, "Rhat"], 3)`,
and the sampler reports
`r rstan::get_num_divergent(stan_fit)`
divergent transitions.
As @tbl-stan-jags-proportion shows,
the mean and the interval endpoints from each program differ from those of the Beta [posterior](bayesian-inference.qmd#def-posterior)
by at most `r round(max(abs(comparison[c("JAGS", "Stan"), ] - rep(comparison["Beta", ], each = 2))), 3)`.
The programs differ in the model code:
the Stan program carries the types and ranges of its variables,
and it is compiled before it draws.
